# QED CockroachDB equivalence pairs

SQL pairs converted from the CockroachDB test corpus of the QED prover.

* Source: https://github.com/qed-solver/prover, `tests/cockroach/{memo,norm,xform}/*.json`
* Commit: `9e9c2621d6d922007694a72f9cc2d5ed0de2eccd` (`9e9c262`, 2026-10-04); all 1,287 files
* Licence of the QED repository: MIT, (c) 2021 The QED Team (see `LICENSE`)
* Converter: `tools/qed_cockroach_to_sql.py` (regenerate with
  `python tools/qed_cockroach_to_sql.py --src <prover>/tests/cockroach`)
* Score: `python tools/qed_cockroach_bench.py` (results: `benchmarks/results/qed-cockroach.json`,
  page: `docs/evals/qed-cockroach.md`)

## Where the cases come from, and which licence applies

QED's paper (extended version, section on the evaluation) says its CockroachDB cases are
query pairs extracted from CockroachDB v23.1.3's optimizer tests: each pair is the plan before
and after one rewrite in CockroachDB's optimizer (`memo`, `norm` and `xform` are QED's folder
names, which match CockroachDB's optimizer packages; that mapping is not stated in QED's
repository). QED's repository ships them as relational-algebra JSON.

What was checked, and what was not:

* The QED repository is MIT. Its `LICENSE` is copied here unchanged. That licence covers QED's
  own files; it says nothing about the licence of the CockroachDB material the cases derive from.
* The QED repository holds no copy of CockroachDB's licence, notice or file headers, and does not
  say which CockroachDB licence applies to the test data. Neither was the CockroachDB source
  checked out here, so the headers of the individual test-data files were **not** verified.
* CockroachDB v23.1 was published under the Business Source License 1.1 (with some enterprise
  code under the CockroachDB Community License), not under an open-source licence. Whatever
  terms apply to CockroachDB's own test text continue to apply to what derives from it. Anyone
  reusing these pairs outside this repository should check CockroachDB's licence for v23.1.3
  themselves.
* To keep the redistributed material small, this folder holds only what QED's MIT repository
  already redistributes, in converted form: SQL generated from the JSON algebra trees, with every
  table and column renamed to `t<i>` and `t<i>_c<j>` (the JSON carries no names). It does **not**
  hold CockroachDB's plan dumps (the `help` field of QED's files), their table or column names,
  their test commentary or their SQL text. Literals that appear in the plans (numbers and short
  strings such as `'aaa'`) are kept, since a rewrite is meaningless without them.
* Original and adapted material are separate: the JSON trees are QED's, extracted from
  CockroachDB's tests; the SQL, the schemas (`CREATE TABLE`) and the skip reasons here are
  generated by `tools/qed_cockroach_to_sql.py` and are this repository's work.

## Files

| file | content |
| --- | --- |
| `qed_cockroach_pairs.jsonl` | one case per line: `name` (`memo/1`, `norm/12`, `xform/3`), `schema_id`, `sql_a`, `sql_b`, `ddl` (CREATE TABLE text), `schemas` (structured: table, columns with type/nullable, keys) |
| `qed_cockroach_schemas.json` | each distinct DDL set by `schema_id` |
| `qed_cockroach_skipped.jsonl` | skipped cases with the reason |
| `summary.json` | counts, with the skip reasons tallied |
| `qed_verdicts.json` | QED's own verdict for each of the 1,287 cases (`provable`, `notprovable` or `error`), from a build of its repository at the pinned commit; the other side of the head-to-head table |

Every case is one CockroachDB rewrite, so the two sides are meant to be equivalent; the corpus
also holds cases QED itself cannot prove (their rewrite depends on facts QED's JSON drops), which
is why a handful of pairs are refuted by a counterexample (see the eval page).

## Conversion notes

The relational part is the Calcite converter's (`tools/qed_to_sql.py`); this converter adds what
CockroachDB needs. Never guess: anything not modelled exactly is a skip with a reason.

* The JSON schemas carry no names: scan `i` reads table `t<i>` with columns `t<i>_c0..`.
* Operator spellings: `EQ NE LT GT LE GE`, `IS` and `<=>` (null-safe equality, how the IR spells an
  index join back to the primary index), `IS NOT`, arithmetic, `AND`/`OR` of one or no operands,
  and `CASE` with its input first.
* Columns of a type with no exact SQL encoding (OID, JSONB, geometry, arrays, UUID, ...) stay in
  the table as opaque BIGINT placeholders and may pass through filters, sorts and joins; a pair
  that reads one in an expression, groups, deduplicates or returns it is skipped.
* Skipped, never guessed: `FUNCTION`/`UDF`/`CONST AGG` (QED's IR keeps no function name),
  `LIMIT`/`OFFSET` without `ORDER BY`, plans that rely on a `CHECK` or computed column the JSON
  schema drops, zero-column relations, `DIV`/`MOD`/`CONCAT`/`SIMILAR TO`, and casts or literals of
  types DuckDB cannot reproduce exactly.
* Ordinals inside a subquery or the right side of an apply join count the enclosing relation's
  columns first. (An earlier version of the converter forgot this for opaque columns: it read an
  ordinal as the inner relation's own column, and converted `norm/337` and ten other pairs
  wrongly. `tests/test_qed_cockroach_to_sql.py` holds the regression.)
